newsitem.title: MACAU: Triads scaring away Macau investors, mogul Ho says.
newsitem.headline: Triads scaring away Macau investors, mogul Ho says.

text.p: Macau casino mogul Stanley Ho said on Friday "Triad" crime gangs in the Portuguese-run enclave were scaring away potential foreign investors.
"Big crimes were never resolved in Macau, not even once," Ho told Reuters, accusing the territory's judges and police of being "too lenient".
Triad activities were "affecting all kinds of (business) possibilities" and the current crime wave could lead to a situation where investors would "just run away", Ho said.
He was speaking to reporters in an interview on the 35th anniversary of his gaming monopoly company Sociedade de Turismo e Diversoes de Macau.
A crackdown on racketeering in casinos in Macau sparked a wave of violent attacks in December.
The violence culminated in an assassination attempt on Macau's top casino police officer, who was shot as he got out of his car. Shootings and grenade bombings have become commonplace.
"I myself will stay, irrespective of the situation," said Ho, a key investor in Macau and one of the enclave's top business figures.
He added he still had confidence in Macau's future because "eventually, the government and the police will find means and ways to rectify and control the situation".
Macau returns to Chinese rule in 1999.
